deliberate_increases.evidence: With the dependency: parity-diff reports 0 capability regressions for both the independence build and the own-entry build against stock ESP-IDF. Without it: 1, persistence.
deliberate_increases.why: Reflex's own key-value store used raw esp_rom_spiflash_* to hold this tier at 1, and that is exactly why it persisted nothing: raw ROM flash access while the CPU executes XIP from the same flash never reaches the medium. The count was protecting a store that silently lost every key it was given — aura pairing impossible, purpose gone by the next boot. Independence measured as subtraction rewarded that; make parity-diff, which measures capability, did not.

deliberate_increases.evidence: 0 esp_ieee802154_* symbols remain in the image (nm on reflex_os.elf). Image 1,087,792 -> 1,077,024 bytes, 10,768 smaller. make blob-check unchanged at 48,566 bytes / 14 symbols, because the PHY floor is exactly what does not move. On hardware: Reflex's MAC brings the radio up, reports the right channel, PAN ID and short address, and its own interrupt reports tx_done=10 tx_abort=0 spurious=0 over 45s with the mesh transmitting through it; ctrl_cfg reads 0x12080080, identical to what ESP-IDF's driver produces.
deliberate_increases.not_yet_proved: Nothing outstanding. Receive was proved once the bench's second C6 came back: 10 minutes of two-board traffic, 129 frames received against 128 sent, zero aborts, zero drops, zero spurious; rx_done falls to 0 when the peer is silenced while transmission continues; and with a shared aura key the mesh authenticates end to end (aura_fail=0, rx_discover=5, peers=1). CONFIG_REFLEX_RADIO_802154_OWN_MAC is now on by default in sdkconfig.defaults.own_entry.
deliberate_increases.what: esp_private/esp_modem_clock.h, esp_private/phy.h, esp_phy_init.h and the libbtbb symbol ieee802154_txon_delay_set, in platform/esp32c6/reflex_802154_mac.c
deliberate_increases.why: Reflex's own 802.15.4 MAC replaces ESP-IDF's ieee802154 component — about 3,240 lines across ten objects, and the owner of the peripheral's state machine — with 229 lines of register programming against bridge-proved constants. What it cannot replace is the RF bring-up: esp_phy_enable and esp_btbb_enable sequence libphy.a and libbtbb.a for calibration and the analog front end, and modem_clock_module_enable is refcounted clock gating shared with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Those three are one-shot silicon bring-up, not an ongoing state machine, and they are Tier D's acknowledged bedrock. The include count treats a whole driver and a one-line bring-up call as equal weight, which is the known weakness of counting surface rather than substance; every other measure moves the right way or not at all.

deliberate_increases.evidence: make independence-own-entry now runs in verify and reports B=2 C=0 D=3 E=0 F=3, on-path 8. The three Tier D entries are the RF bring-up blobs and nothing else: libphy.a via esp_phy_enable and two headerless libbtbb symbols.
deliberate_increases.what: esp_private/phy.h and the libbtbb externs ieee802154_txon_delay_set and bt_bb_v2_init_cmplx, in platform/esp32c6/reflex_802154_mac.c
deliberate_increases.why: A baseline correction, not a regression. The 2026-09-10 decision that accepted Reflex's own MAC recorded this tier going to 4, but the baseline file was never updated from 1, and nothing caught it because `independence-own-entry` was not in `make verify` — the one configuration the independence claim rests on was ungated. With the gate added and bt_bb_v2_init_cmplx classified, the honest number is 3: one better than the accepted 4, because esp_private/esp_modem_clock.h and esp_phy_init.h have since been taken.

measurement_corrections.consequence: The claim that Tier C was clear for the own-entry build was wrong and is retracted. Measured honestly it is 4 there, 8 here. check_independence.py counts externs now, so lowering the number by changing declaration style is no longer possible.
measurement_corrections.what: intr_handler_set / intr_handler_get / intr_handler_get_arg, reached by local extern
measurement_corrections.why: Not a regression — these dependencies were always there and the tool could not see them. It read #include lines only, so anything declared with a local extern was invisible, and this codebase declares symbols that way deliberately for ROM entry points. These three are not ROM: they are ESP-IDF C in components/riscv/interrupt.c, and a comment in reflex_hal_esp32c6.c claimed they lived in mask ROM, which is false. Reflex's allocator registers into ESP-IDF's handler table and reflex_trap_handler reads it to dispatch every interrupt Reflex does not own.

measurement_corrections.consequence: The two configurations now carry separate baselines, because they genuinely have different numbers and a single flat baseline could only be right about one of them. Reported to the user as pre-existing drift when first seen; that was wrong, it was caused by this change and is correct.
measurement_corrections.why: Not a removal. That include sits behind #ifdef REFLEX_OWN_ENTRY, and until the tool could resolve that symbol it counted both branches — so the independence build, which never compiles the include, was charged for it. Reading REFLEX_OWN_ENTRY back from the build's own compile_commands.json resolves it to not-defined there and the include drops out. The same change resolves it to defined for build_own_entry, where the include is real and Tier F is correspondingly 3.

note: Ratchet baseline, per build configuration. Lower is the only legal direction. Regenerate deliberately with tools/check_independence.py --update [--build <dir>].
